row.scenario: slice-2 query fixture: "what editor do I prefer?" recalls "User prefers vim for editing"
row.required_outcome: The natural question finds the note by the words the question and the note share: `editor`, a whole token of the title, and `prefer` as the beginning of the title's `preference` and the body's `prefers` (the `unicode61` table's prefix query, 09 §6.5, LQ17). Step 1 carries `term` and `prefix`. Supports matrix rows 12 and 13 and plan 3.3's per-turn recall test; fixture 26 is the body-only variant.

design: §5 step 3: union of terms, never the whole message ANDed

§5 step 4 (03 rev 7.8, 09 §6.5.2): the `unicode61` table takes every term, as a prefix query when its last token has three or more characters; a word-beginning hit has a trigram-only hit's coverage weight, below a whole-token hit, and is reported as `prefix`; no stemmer
notes_for_implementer: One note, one decoy. Before LQ17 this file said the note was found only through the trigram table and that plain `unicode61` returned nothing; that was the G23 reproduction under the whole-message AND the design removed. With the terms ORed, `editor` is a whole token of the title "Editor preference", so the word table alone finds the note, and `prefer*` finds the title's `preference` and the body's `prefers` as word beginnings: step 1 carries `term` and `prefix`. `what`/`do`/`i` are stop words and match nothing; `editor` does not match the body's `editing` (neither begins the other). `unicode61_only_would_return` records that the word table alone now returns the note; the loader does not run it. Step 3 is the same question with a stop-word-free phrasing (`preferred*` matches nothing; `editor` does); step 4 the whole-token form, which must carry `term`. Fixture 26 is the body-only test: there the title does not help.
